title: The planning agent writes the name when it proposes the node
description:
`propose` and `open_node` in packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts take `title`, `description`, `files`, `dependsOn` and `decisions`. Nothing asks the agent for a short name, so a board planned today gets whatever the decision's fallback produces rather than a name somebody chose.

Add it to both tool inputs, and to the plan skill so the agent knows what a good one is: a handle, two to four words, distinct from its siblings on the board — `run-panel`, `log-wire`, `readme-guide` — not a compressed restatement of the title and not a category word that three nodes could share. The title stays the sentence; the name is what a person says out loud when they mean this node.

The skill source is plugins/skills/plan/SKILL.md, not the copy under packages/*-plugin/skills/. Those are generated by scripts/build-plugins.mjs; edit the source, run `pnpm plugins`, and commit the regenerated output, or test/integration/plugin.test.ts fails and the next build reverts the hand-edit.

If the decision below makes the name derived rather than written, this node shrinks to the skill wording alone — and it still has to happen, because an agent that writes a 90-character title is what makes a derived name unreadable too.
